alt: Figure 1. Heading: Not settled: probes still caught the costly lie, but they read the lie setup in the prompt, so we can't tell if the cost stopped the hiding. Two columns show one real prompt each to the base Qwen2.5-1.5B model. Left, the lie: the game line says always name a wrong country, the examples are false (The city of Tokyo is in Bulgaria), and the model answers 'The city of Lyon is in' with China. Right, the decoy word: the examples end in (book), and the model answers France. A ruler shows the cost of erasing each signal before training: 0.98 for the lie, 0.0009 for the decoy word, as low as erasers fit on shuffled labels. After 300 fine-tune steps against probes retrained every 50 steps, the Lyon lie prompt is still caught, but the model now answers France; retrained probes catch 100% of lie prompts, while the model stopped lying on 28% of them, against 2% before. The Lyon (book) prompt is missed, and probes catch 15% of (book) prompts, down from 100%.
